entries.reason: on a single-precision setup the targets are approached a sample at a time, which is what the host does and the header does not say: the rate is the fraction of the distance left, and the threshold is what is close enough to land on
entries.effect: each sample of each vDSP_biquadm call after it, every named coefficient moves by (target - coefficient) * (1 - interp_rate), or lands exactly on the target when what is left is at most interp_threshold; a rate of 0 or a threshold at or above the distance puts the target in place before the first sample. Measured with a b0 going from 1 to 9 and a threshold of 0.25: a rate of 0.5 has the samples of one call answer 1, 5, 7, 8, 8.5, 9, 9, 9, a rate of 0.1 answers 1, 8.2, 9 and a rate of 0.9 answers 1, 1.8, 2.52, 3.168 In a cascade the walk differs from a single section's: a coefficient lands on its target when what is left of the distance is at most interp_threshold *and* every section after it has landed too, so the snap travels backwards through the cascade. Measured over eleven host cases at rates of 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75 and thresholds of 0.1 to 0.5, and the port answers every one of them
